section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a conic section by showing a 3D cone being sliced by a 2D plane. Define the 'Elliptical Slice' and pose the central question: Why does this specific 2D curve satisfy the mathematical definition of an ellipse?
section_1.example: An animated 'Professor Penguin' slices a cone-shaped block of ice with a laser, creating a slanted cross-section. He challenges the viewer to prove it's a perfect ellipse.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The String & The Sphere
section_2.content: Review two crucial geometric rules: 1. The definition of an ellipse (the sum of distances to two fixed foci is constant). 2. The Tangent Segment Theorem (tangent lines drawn from a single point to a sphere are always equal in length).
section_2.example: Visualizing a gardener using a loose loop of string around two pegs to draw a flowerbed, followed by a 3D animation showing two tangent lines from a floating point touching a sphere at equal distances.

section_3.title: The Magic Trick: Inserting the Spheres
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres.' Place two spheres (one small, one large) inside the cone so that they are each tangent to the cone's inner surface and also touch the cutting plane at exactly one point.
section_3.example: Imagine dropping two crystal balls into the ice-cone. The points where they touch the 'laser-cut' plane are labeled F1 and F2 (the future foci).

section_4.title: The Geometric Bridge
section_4.content: Pick a random point P on the elliptical slice. Trace two paths: one to the sphere's contact point on the plane (PF) and one along the cone's surface to the circle where the sphere touches the cone (the 'rim'). Show that these segments are equal because of the Tangent Segment Theorem.
section_4.example: A tiny 'Ant' starts at point P on the edge of the slice. Whether he walks to the contact point of the sphere or slides down the cone to the sphere's 'equator,' the distance traveled is identical.

section_5.title: The Grand Proof
section_5.content: Demonstrate that the sum of the distances from point P to both spheres' contact points (PF1 + PF2) is equal to the fixed distance between the two 'rim' circles along the cone's slant height. Since this distance doesn't change regardless of where P is, the curve is proven to be an ellipse.
section_5.example: The two segments PF1 and PF2 are highlighted in glowing colors. As P moves around the ellipse, the total length of the 'glowing line' stays perfectly constant, matching a fixed segment on the cone's wall.

section_6.title: Application: From Ice Cones to Orbits
section_6.content: Briefly explain how this 3D perspective applies to other conic sections (parabolas and hyperbolas) by changing the angle of the plane. Conclude with how this geometry governs the motion of planets and satellites.
section_6.example: The Professor Penguin uses his laser to tilt the plane further, transforming the ellipse into a parabola. A satellite is then shown orbiting Earth in an elliptical path, governed by the same focal geometry proven by the spheres.

Show a blue sphere (#0000FF) and demonstrate that all tangent segments from an external point to it are equal length (#00FF00).

section_3.title: The Magic Trick: Inserting the Spheres
lecture_lines: Nest two spheres between the cone and plane.
Plane contact points will become our two foci.
We call these the Dandelin Spheres.
animations: Re-display the 3D cone (#888888) and slicing plane (#FFFFFF).
Insert a small sphere (#FFD700) above the plane, tangent to both the cone and the plane.
Mark its contact point on the plane as 'F1' (#FF0000).
Insert a larger sphere (#FFD700) below the plane, tangent to both.
Mark its contact point on the plane as 'F2' (#FF0000).

section_4.title: The Geometric Bridge
lecture_lines: Pick any point P on the ellipse's edge.
Link P to the sphere's contact point.
Trace from P along the cone's surface.
These two segments are equal tangent lengths.
This bridge connects the plane and cone.
animations: Pick a point 'P' (#FFFFFF) on the intersection curve.
Draw a line from 'P' to 'F1' and a line along the cone to where the top sphere touches it.
Highlight these two segments in orange (#FFA500) to show they are equal tangent lengths.

section_5.title: The Grand Proof
lecture_lines: Sum the distances from P to both foci.
This sum equals a fixed cone slant distance.
Slant distance between spheres never changes.
Thus, the total distance from P is constant.
This proves the curve is a perfect ellipse.
animations: Show that PF1 equals the segment from P to the top circle (Q1).
Show that PF2 equals the segment from P to the bottom circle (Q2).
Combine these to show PF1 + PF2 = Q1Q2, which is the slant distance between the two circles.
Slide point P around the ellipse; show the distance Q1Q2 between circles stays constant.
Display 'Constant Sum = Ellipse' (#FFFFFF) with a celebratory glow on the curve.

section_6.title: Application: From Ice Cones to Orbits
lecture_lines: Tilting the plane creates other conic sections.
This geometry governs how planets orbit stars.
3D shapes explain our 2D mathematical world.
animations: Tilt the slicing plane to show a Parabola (#FF00FF) and a Hyperbola (#00FF00).
Transform the scene into a planet (#ADD8E6) orbiting a sun (#FFFF00) in an elliptical path.
Final text: 'The Geometry of the Universe' (#FFFFFF).

outline.title: The Mystery of the Slice
outline.content: Introduce the concept of a conic section by showing a 3D cone being sliced by a 2D plane. Define the 'Elliptical Slice' and pose the central question: Why does this specific 2D curve satisfy the mathematical definition of an ellipse?
outline.example: An animated 'Professor Penguin' slices a cone-shaped block of ice with a laser, creating a slanted cross-section. He challenges the viewer to prove it's a perfect ellipse.

storyboard.title: The Mystery of the Slice
lecture_lines: Imagine slicing a cone with a flat plane.
This intersection creates a perfect elliptical curve.
Why does this slice follow the ellipse formula?
animations: Fade in a 3D cone (#888888) and a slicing plane (#FFFFFF) at an angle.
Draw the intersection curve (the slice) in bright cyan (#00FFFF).
Rotate the camera to show the slice is an oval shape on the plane.
Fade out the cone and plane, leaving only the cyan oval.
Center the cyan oval and add text 'Why is this an Ellipse?' (#FFFFFF).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "The Magic Trick: Inserting the Spheres"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Nest two spheres between the cone and plane.",
            "Plane contact points will become our two foci.",
            "We call these the Dandelin Spheres."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Define colors
        CONE_COLOR = "#888888"
        PLANE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        SPHERE_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        FOCI_COLOR = "#FF0000"

        # 3D Construction Group
        # Since we are in a 2D Scene, we'll use a VGroup and rotate it to simulate 3D
        three_d_view = VGroup()

        # 1. Cone (Visual representation)
        # We'll use a double cone for the full effect, but focusing on the top part for now
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=4.0, direction=UP, 
                   fill_opacity=0.1, color=CONE_COLOR, stroke_width=1)
        cone.rotate(PI, axis=RIGHT) # Point down for "ice cream cone" feel
        cone.move_to(ORIGIN)
        three_d_view.add(cone)

        # 2. Slicing Plane
        # A tilted plane that intersects the cone
        plane = Rectangle(width=4, height=4, fill_opacity=0.2, 
                          fill_color=PLANE_COLOR, color=PLANE_COLOR)
        plane.rotate(60 * DEGREES, axis=RIGHT)
        plane.rotate(10 * DEGREES, axis=UP)
        plane.move_to(UP * 0.2)
        three_d_view.add(plane)

        # Position the 3D view in the visual area (right side)
        # Area A2 to F6 to respect Belief B021
        self.place_in_area(three_d_view, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # Small Sphere (above plane)
        # Positioned to be tangent to cone walls and plane
        small_sphere = Sphere(radius=0.4, fill_opacity=0.6, color=SPHERE_COLOR)
        # Offset calculation (manual adjustment for visual tangency in 3D perspective)
        small_sphere.move_to(three_d_view.get_center() + UP * 1.0 + RIGHT * 0.1)
        
        # Large Sphere (below plane)
        large_sphere = Sphere(radius=0.9, fill_opacity=0.6, color=SPHERE_COLOR)
        large_sphere.move_to(three_d_view.get_center() + DOWN * 0.8 + LEFT * 0.1)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(small_sphere, shift=DOWN),
            FadeIn(large_sphere, shift=UP)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(FOCI_COLOR)
        )

        # Contact Points (Foci)
        # F1: Contact point of small sphere and plane
        f1_pos = small_sphere.get_center() + DOWN * 0.4 + LEFT * 0.05 # Adjusted for tilt
        f1 = Dot(point=f1_pos, color=FOCI_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        f1_label = MathTex("F_1", color=FOCI_COLOR, font_size=24)
        # Using Belief B001: Offset label
        f1_label.next_to(f1, UR, buff=0.1)

        # F2: Contact point of large sphere and plane
        f2_pos = large_sphere.get_center() + UP * 0.9 + RIGHT * 0.05 # Adjusted for tilt
        f2 = Dot(point=f2_pos, color=FOCI_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        f2_label = MathTex("F_2", color=FOCI_COLOR, font_size=24)
        f2_label.next_to(f2, DL, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Create(f1), Write(f1_label),
            Create(f2), Write(f2_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SPHERE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Highlight spheres
        self.play(
            small_sphere.animate.set_stroke(SPHERE_COLOR, width=2),
            large_sphere.animate.set_stroke(SPHERE_COLOR, width=2)
        )

        # Label the spheres
        dandelin_label = Text("Dandelin Spheres", font_size=18, color=SPHERE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(dandelin_label, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(dandelin_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Application: From Ice Cones to Orbits"
        lines = [
            "Tilting the plane creates other conic sections.",
            "This geometry governs how planets orbit stars.",
            "3D shapes explain our 2D mathematical world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors from animation description
        color_parabola = "#FF00FF"
        color_hyperbola = "#00FF00"
        color_planet = "#ADD8E6"
        color_sun = "#FFFF00"
        color_text = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Representing a cone via cross-section
        cone_l = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F2"], color=GREY_B)
        cone_r = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F6"], color=GREY_B)
        cone = VGroup(cone_l, cone_r)
        
        # Slicing Plane line
        plane = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D5"], color=WHITE)
        plane_label = Text("Plane", font_size=18).next_to(plane, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane), Write(plane_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Parabola Animation
        # Define a parabola relative to the grid
        parabola = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.8 * x**2 - 0.5, 
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], 
            color=color_parabola
        )
        self.place_in_area(parabola, "C3", "E5")
        parabola_label = Text("Parabola", color=color_parabola, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6),
            FadeIn(parabola),
            Write(parabola_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Hyperbola Animation
        hyperbola_top = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.3), 
            x_range=[-1, 1], 
            color=color_hyperbola
        )
        hyperbola_bot = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: -np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.3), 
            x_range=[-1, 1], 
            color=color_hyperbola
        )
        hyperbola = VGroup(hyperbola_top, hyperbola_bot)
        self.place_in_area(hyperbola, "C3", "E5")
        
        hyperbola_label = Text("Hyperbola", color=color_hyperbola, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6),
            FadeOut(parabola),
            FadeOut(parabola_label),
            FadeIn(hyperbola),
            Write(hyperbola_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup for transition
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(plane_label),
            FadeOut(hyperbola), FadeOut(hyperbola_label),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Orbital system
        # Center of ellipse at D4, Sun at focus D3 (distance = 1.0)
        # a=1.5, c=1.0 => b = sqrt(1.5^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(1.25) approx 1.118
        # width = 2a = 3.0, height = 2b = 2.236
        orbit_path = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=2.236, color=BLUE_E).set_stroke(opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(orbit_path, "D4")
        
        sun = Dot(color=color_sun, radius=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(sun, "D3") # Focus
        sun_label = Text("Sun", color=color_sun, font_size=20).next_to(sun, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        planet = Dot(color=color_planet, radius=0.12)
        planet_label = Text("Planet", color=color_planet, font_size=18)
        
        # Setup orbital movement
        orbit_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        planet.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(orbit_path.point_from_proportion(orbit_tracker.get_value() % 1)))
        planet_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(planet, UR, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(Create(orbit_path), FadeIn(sun), Write(sun_label))
        self.add(planet, planet_label)
        self.play(orbit_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(orbit_path), FadeOut(sun), FadeOut(sun_label),
            FadeOut(planet), FadeOut(planet_label),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for multi-word labels
        final_msg = Text("The Geometry of the Universe", color=color_text, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_msg, "B2", "E6")
        
        self.play(Write(final_msg))
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=1)
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # End of section
        self.play(FadeOut(final_msg), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Application: From Ice Cones to Orbits"
        lines = [
            "Tilting the plane creates other conic sections.",
            "This geometry governs how planets orbit stars.",
            "3D shapes explain our 2D mathematical world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors from animation description
        color_parabola = "#FF00FF"
        color_hyperbola = "#00FF00"
        color_planet = "#ADD8E6"
        color_sun = "#FFFF00"
        color_text = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Representing a cone via cross-section
        cone_l = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F2"], color=GREY_B)
        cone_r = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F6"], color=GREY_B)
        cone = VGroup(cone_l, cone_r)
        
        # Slicing Plane line
        plane = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D5"], color=WHITE)
        plane_label = Text("Plane", font_size=18).next_to(plane, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane), Write(plane_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Parabola Animation
        # Define a parabola relative to the grid
        parabola = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.8 * x**2 - 0.5, 
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], 
            color=color_parabola
        )
        self.place_in_area(parabola, "C3", "E5")
        parabola_label = Text("Parabola", color=color_parabola, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6),
            FadeIn(parabola),
            Write(parabola_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Hyperbola Animation
        hyperbola_top = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.3), 
            x_range=[-1, 1], 
            color=color_hyperbola
        )
        hyperbola_bot = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: -np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.3), 
            x_range=[-1, 1], 
            color=color_hyperbola
        )
        hyperbola = VGroup(hyperbola_top, hyperbola_bot)
        self.place_in_area(hyperbola, "C3", "E5")
        
        hyperbola_label = Text("Hyperbola", color=color_hyperbola, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_label, "B5")

            Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6),
            FadeOut(parabola),
            FadeOut(parabola_label),
            FadeIn(hyperbola),
            Write(hyperbola_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup for transition
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(plane_label),
            FadeOut(hyperbola), FadeOut(hyperbola_label),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Orbital system
        # Center of ellipse at D4, Sun at focus D3 (distance = 1.0)
        # a=1.5, c=1.0 => b = sqrt(1.5^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(1.25) approx 1.118
        # width = 2a = 3.0, height = 2b = 2.236
        orbit_path = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=2.236, color=BLUE_E).set_stroke(opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(orbit_path, "D4")
        
        sun = Dot(color=color_sun, radius=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(sun, "D3") # Focus
        sun_label = Text("Sun", color=color_sun, font_size=20).next_to(sun, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        planet = Dot(color=color_planet, radius=0.12)
        planet_label = Text("Planet", color=color_planet, font_size=18)
        
        # Setup orbital movement
        orbit_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        planet.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(orbit_path.point_from_proportion(orbit_tracker.get_value() % 1)))
        planet_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(planet, UR, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(Create(orbit_path), FadeIn(sun), Write(sun_label))
        self.add(planet, planet_label)
        self.play(orbit_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(orbit_path), FadeOut(sun), FadeOut(sun_label),
            FadeOut(planet), FadeOut(planet_label),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for multi-word labels
        final_msg = Text("The Geometry of the Universe", color=color_text, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_msg, "B2", "E6")
        
        self.play(Write(final_msg))
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=1)
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # End of section
        self.play(FadeOut(final_msg), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # Initial Setup
        self.setup_layout("The Grand Proof", [
            "Sum the distances from P to both foci.",
            "This sum equals a fixed cone slant distance.",
            "Slant distance between spheres never changes.",
            "Thus, the total distance from P is constant.",
            "This proves the curve is a perfect ellipse."
        ])

        # Define basic geometry colors
        color_p = WHITE
        color_f1 = CYAN
        color_f2 = YELLOW
        color_plane = ORANGE
        color_cone = GREY_B
        color_sphere = GREY_D
        color_slant = PURPLE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Cone cross-section
        apex = self.grid["A4"]
        wall_l = Line(apex, self.grid["F2"], color=color_cone)
        wall_r = Line(apex, self.grid["F6"], color=color_cone)
        self.add(wall_l, wall_r)

        # Plane line (representing the ellipse)
        plane_start = self.grid["B3"]
        plane_end = self.grid["E5"]
        plane_line = Line(plane_start, plane_end, color=color_plane)
        self.add(plane_line)

        # Spheres (Circles tangent to walls and plane)
        # Manually positioned for visual clarity
        s1_center = self.grid["B4"] + DOWN * 0.1
        s1 = Circle(radius=0.45, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(s1_center)
        s2_center = self.grid["D4"] + DOWN * 0.35
        s2 = Circle(radius=0.85, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(s2_center)
        self.add(s1, s2)

        p_dot = Dot(color=color_p)

        q2_pos = wall_l.point_from_proportion(0.75)

        # Note: In a 2D projection, PQ lines won't always coincide with the wall,

        pq1_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(p_dot.get_center(), q1.get_center(), color=color_f1, stroke_dash_array=[0.1, 0.1]))
        pq2_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(p_dot.get_center(), q2.get_center(), color=color_f2, stroke_dash_array=[0.1, 0.1]))

section_1.title: The Mystery of the Slice
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a conic section by showing a 3D cone being sliced by a 2D plane. Define the 'Elliptical Slice' and pose the central question: Why does this specific 2D curve satisfy the mathematical definition of an ellipse?
section_1.example: An animated 'Professor Penguin' slices a cone-shaped block of ice with a laser, creating a slanted cross-section. He challenges the viewer to prove it's a perfect ellipse.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The String & The Sphere
section_2.content: Review two crucial geometric rules: 1. The definition of an ellipse (the sum of distances to two fixed foci is constant). 2. The Tangent Segment Theorem (tangent lines drawn from a single point to a sphere are always equal in length).
section_2.example: Visualizing a gardener using a loose loop of string around two pegs to draw a flowerbed, followed by a 3D animation showing two tangent lines from a floating point touching a sphere at equal distances.

section_3.title: The Magic Trick: Inserting the Spheres
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres.' Place two spheres (one small, one large) inside the cone so that they are each tangent to the cone's inner surface and also touch the cutting plane at exactly one point.
section_3.example: Imagine dropping two crystal balls into the ice-cone. The points where they touch the 'laser-cut' plane are labeled F1 and F2 (the future foci).

section_4.title: The Geometric Bridge
section_4.content: Pick a random point P on the elliptical slice. Trace two paths: one to the sphere's contact point on the plane (PF) and one along the cone's surface to the circle where the sphere touches the cone (the 'rim'). Show that these segments are equal because of the Tangent Segment Theorem.
section_4.example: A tiny 'Ant' starts at point P on the edge of the slice. Whether he walks to the contact point of the sphere or slides down the cone to the sphere's 'equator,' the distance traveled is identical.

section_5.title: The Grand Proof
section_5.content: Demonstrate that the sum of the distances from point P to both spheres' contact points (PF1 + PF2) is equal to the fixed distance between the two 'rim' circles along the cone's slant height. Since this distance doesn't change regardless of where P is, the curve is proven to be an ellipse.
section_5.example: The two segments PF1 and PF2 are highlighted in glowing colors. As P moves around the ellipse, the total length of the 'glowing line' stays perfectly constant, matching a fixed segment on the cone's wall.

section_6.title: Application: From Ice Cones to Orbits
section_6.content: Briefly explain how this 3D perspective applies to other conic sections (parabolas and hyperbolas) by changing the angle of the plane. Conclude with how this geometry governs the motion of planets and satellites.
section_6.example: The Professor Penguin uses his laser to tilt the plane further, transforming the ellipse into a parabola. A satellite is then shown orbiting Earth in an elliptical path, governed by the same focal geometry proven by the spheres.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data for the scene
        title = "The Mystery of the Slice"
        lines = [
            "- Imagine slicing a cone with a flat plane.",
            "- This intersection creates a perfect elliptical curve.",
            "- Why does this slice follow the ellipse formula?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        CONE_COLOR = "#888888"
        PLANE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        SLICE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        TEXT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Imagine slicing a cone with a flat plane.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a 2D perspective representation of a cone
        cone_base = Ellipse(width=3, height=0.6, color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        cone_base.shift(DOWN * 1.5)
        cone_sides = Polygon([-1.5, -1.5, 0], [0, 1.5, 0], [1.5, -1.5, 0], color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.1)
        cone = VGroup(cone_sides, cone_base)
        self.place_in_area(cone, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Create a slicing plane (parallelogram)
        plane = Polygon(
            [-2.5, 0.5, 0], [1.5, 1.5, 0], [2.5, -0.5, 0], [-1.5, -1.5, 0],
            color=PLANE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        # Visual adjustment to make it look like it's intersecting the middle
        plane.shift(UP * 0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), FadeIn(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # This intersection creates a perfect elliptical curve.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Tilted ellipse representing the slice
        slice_curve = Ellipse(width=1.6, height=0.6, color=SLICE_COLOR, stroke_width=5)
        slice_curve.rotate(14 * DEGREES)
        self.place_in_area(slice_curve, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        slice_curve.shift(UP * 0.4 + RIGHT * 0.1) # Align with the plane's tilt
        
        self.play(Create(slice_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Why does this slice follow the ellipse formula?
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Simulate camera rotation: transform components to face-on view
        # The slice becomes a standard oval
        final_ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.5, height=2.2, color=SLICE_COLOR, stroke_width=5)
        self.place_in_area(final_ellipse, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Rotate the view:

        self.play(
            Transform(slice_curve, final_ellipse),
            cone.animate.set_opacity(0),
            plane.animate.set_opacity(0),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.remove(cone, plane)
        
        # Final Question Text (Applying B002: Span multiple columns)

        self.play(Write(question_text))

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: The String & The Sphere"
        lines = [
            "Ellipses have two foci with constant distance sum.",
            "Tangents from one point to a sphere are equal.",
            "These rules help unlock the cone's secret."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Colors
        color_ellipse = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        color_foci = "#FF0000"    # Red
        color_lines = "#FFFF00"   # Yellow
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_ellipse)
        
        # Ellipse
        # Using a=2, b=1.25 -> c = 1.56
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=4.0, height=2.5, color=color_ellipse)
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, 'B2', 'E6')
        center_pos = ellipse.get_center()
        c = 1.56
        
        focus1_pos = center_pos + LEFT * c
        focus2_pos = center_pos + RIGHT * c
        
        focus1 = Dot(focus1_pos, color=color_foci)
        focus2 = Dot(focus2_pos, color=color_foci)
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for multi-word Text labels
        foci_label = Text("Foci Locations", font_size=24, color=color_foci)
        self.place_in_area(foci_label, 'A3', 'A5')
        
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.play(FadeIn(focus1, focus2), Write(foci_label))
        
        # Constant sum demonstration
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(PI/4)
        
        def get_point_on_ellipse():
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            return center_pos + np.array([2 * np.cos(theta), 1.25 * np.sin(theta), 0])
        
        moving_point = Dot(get_point_on_ellipse(), color=WHITE)
        moving_point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_point_on_ellipse()))
        
        line1 = Line(focus1_pos, get_point_on_ellipse(), color=color_lines)
        line2 = Line(focus2_pos, get_point_on_ellipse(), color=color_lines)
        
        line1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([focus1_pos, get_point_on_ellipse()]))
        line2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([focus2_pos, get_point_on_ellipse()]))
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for long MathTex expressions
        sum_text = MathTex("d_1 + d_2 = \\text{constant}", font_size=32, color=color_lines)
        self.place_in_area(sum_text, 'F2', 'F6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(moving_point, line1, line2), Write(sum_text))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/4 + 2*PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        color_sphere = "#0000FF"   # Blue
        color_tangent = "#00FF00"  # Green
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_sphere),
            FadeOut(ellipse, focus1, focus2, foci_label, moving_point, line1, line2, sum_text)
        )
        
        # "Sphere"
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.5, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sphere.set_fill(color_sphere, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B3', 'E5')
        sphere_center = sphere.get_center()
        
        # External Point
        # B021: Maintain gap from lecture text (Column 1)
        p_pos = self.grid['C6']
        point_p = Dot(p_pos, color=WHITE)
        
        # Calculate Tangent Points
        d_val = np.linalg.norm(p_pos - sphere_center)
        r_val = 1.5
        local_p = p_pos - sphere_center
        angle_p = np.arctan2(local_p[1], local_p[0])
        alpha = np.arccos(r_val / d_val)
        
        t1_pos = sphere_center + np.array([r_val * np.cos(angle_p + alpha), r_val * np.sin(angle_p + alpha), 0])
        t2_pos = sphere_center + np.array([r_val * np.cos(angle_p - alpha), r_val * np.sin(angle_p - alpha), 0])
        
        tangent1 = Line(p_pos, t1_pos, color=color_tangent)
        tangent2 = Line(p_pos, t2_pos, color=color_tangent)
        
        l1_label = MathTex("L_1", font_size=28, color=color_tangent).next_to(tangent1, UP, buff=0.1)
        l2_label = MathTex("L_2", font_size=28, color=color_tangent).next_to(tangent2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        equal_text = MathTex("L_1 = L_2", font_size=32, color=color_tangent)
        self.place_in_area(equal_text, 'F3', 'F5')
        
        sphere_label = Text("3D Sphere Model", font_size=24, color=color_sphere)
        self.place_in_area(sphere_label, 'A3', 'A5')

        self.play(Create(sphere), Write(sphere_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(point_p))
        self.play(Create(tangent1), Create(tangent2))
        self.play(Write(l1_label), Write(l2_label))
        self.play(Write(equal_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup or hold

        SPHERE_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        FOCI_COLOR = "#FF0000"

        # 3D Construction Group
        # Since we are in a 2D Scene, we'll use a VGroup and rotate it to simulate 3D
        three_d_view = VGroup()

        # 1. Cone (Visual representation)
        # We'll use a double cone for the full effect, but focusing on the top part for now
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=4.0, direction=UP, 
                   fill_opacity=0.1, color=CONE_COLOR, stroke_width=1)
        cone.rotate(PI, axis=RIGHT) # Point down for "ice cream cone" feel

        three_d_view.add(cone)

        # 2. Slicing Plane
        # A tilted plane that intersects the cone
        plane = Rectangle(width=4, height=4, fill_opacity=0.2, 
                          fill_color=PLANE_COLOR, color=PLANE_COLOR)
        plane.rotate(60 * DEGREES, axis=RIGHT)
        plane.rotate(10 * DEGREES, axis=UP)
        plane.move_to(UP * 0.2)
        three_d_view.add(plane)

        # Position the 3D view in the visual area (right side)
        # Area A2 to F6 to respect Belief B021
        self.place_in_area(three_d_view, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        small_sphere = Sphere(radius=0.4, fill_opacity=0.6, color=SPHERE_COLOR)

        # Large Sphere (below plane)

        large_sphere.move_to(three_d_view.get_center() + DOWN * 0.8 + LEFT * 0.1)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(small_sphere, shift=DOWN),
            FadeIn(large_sphere, shift=UP)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        f1 = Dot(point=f1_pos, color=FOCI_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        f1_label = MathTex("F_1", color=FOCI_COLOR, font_size=24)
        # Using Belief B001: Offset label
        f1_label.next_to(f1, UR, buff=0.1)

        # F2: Contact point of large sphere and plane
        f2_pos = large_sphere.get_center() + UP * 0.9 + RIGHT * 0.05 # Adjusted for tilt
        f2 = Dot(point=f2_pos, color=FOCI_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        f2_label = MathTex("F_2", color=FOCI_COLOR, font_size=24)
        f2_label.next_to(f2, DL, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Create(f1), Write(f1_label),
            Create(f2), Write(f2_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SPHERE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Highlight spheres
        self.play(
            small_sphere.animate.set_stroke(SPHERE_COLOR, width=2),
            large_sphere.animate.set_stroke(SPHERE_COLOR, width=2)

        # Label the spheres

        self.place_at_grid(dandelin_label, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(dandelin_label))
        self.wait(2)

            "This sum equals a fixed cone slant distance.",

        ])

        color_p = WHITE
        color_f1 = TEAL

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # Plane line (representing the ellipse)
        plane_start = self.grid["B3"]
        plane_end = self.grid["E5"]
        plane_line = Line(plane_start, plane_end, color=color_plane)
        self.add(plane_line)

        # Spheres (Circles tangent to walls and plane)
        # Manually positioned for visual clarity
        s1_center = self.grid["B4"] + DOWN * 0.1
        s1 = Circle(radius=0.45, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(s1_center)
        s2_center = self.grid["D4"] + DOWN * 0.35
        s2 = Circle(radius=0.85, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(s2_center)
        self.add(s1, s2)

        # Focal points (where spheres touch the plane)
        f1_pos = plane_line.point_from_proportion(0.2)
        f2_pos = plane_line.point_from_proportion(0.8)
        f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=color_f1)
        f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=color_f2)
        f1_label = MathTex("F_1", color=color_f1, font_size=20).next_to(f1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        f2_label = MathTex("F_2", color=color_f2, font_size=20).next_to(f2, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Point P on the ellipse
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        p_dot = Dot(color=color_p)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(plane_line.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value())))
        p_label = MathTex("P", color=color_p, font_size=24)
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        # PF1 and PF2 segments
        pf1_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(p_dot.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color=color_f1, stroke_width=4))

        self.play(

            Create(pf1_line),
            Create(pf2_line)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Introduce points Q1 and Q2 on the slant height
        # In Dandelin's proof, PF1 = PQ1 and PF2 = PQ2 where Q is on the rim circles.
        # We visualize these Q points on the wall generator.
        
        # Q1 and Q2 on the wall (rim circle contact points)
        q1_pos = wall_l.point_from_proportion(0.25)
        q2_pos = wall_l.point_from_proportion(0.75)
        q1 = Dot(q1_pos, color=color_f1)
        q2 = Dot(q2_pos, color=color_f2)
        q1_label = MathTex("Q_1", color=color_f1, font_size=20).next_to(q1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        q2_label = MathTex("Q_2", color=color_f2, font_size=20).next_to(q2, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # PQ1 and PQ2 as dashed segments to show mapping (Tangent Equality)
        pq1_line = always_redraw(lambda: DashedLine(p_dot.get_center(), q1.get_center(), color=color_f1, dash_length=0.1))
        pq2_line = always_redraw(lambda: DashedLine(p_dot.get_center(), q2.get_center(), color=color_f2, dash_length=0.1))

        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.play(FadeIn(q1, q1_label, q2, q2_label), Create(pq1_line), Create(pq2_line))

        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6),
            FadeOut(parabola),
            FadeOut(parabola_label),
            FadeIn(hyperbola),
            Write(hyperbola_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup for transition
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(plane_label),
            FadeOut(hyperbola), FadeOut(hyperbola_label),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Orbital system
        # Center of ellipse at D4, Sun at focus D3 (distance = 1.0)
        # a=1.5, c=1.0 => b = sqrt(1.5^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(1.25) approx 1.118
        # width = 2a = 3.0, height = 2b = 2.236
        orbit_path = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=2.236, color=BLUE_E).set_stroke(opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(orbit_path, "D4")
        
        sun = Dot(color=color_sun, radius=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(sun, "D3") # Focus
        sun_label = Text("Sun", color=color_sun, font_size=20).next_to(sun, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        planet = Dot(color=color_planet, radius=0.12)
        planet_label = Text("Planet", color=color_planet, font_size=18)
        
        # Setup orbital movement
        orbit_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        planet.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(orbit_path.point_from_proportion(orbit_tracker.get_value() % 1)))
        planet_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(planet, UR, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(Create(orbit_path), FadeIn(sun), Write(sun_label))
        self.add(planet, planet_label)
        self.play(orbit_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(orbit_path), FadeOut(sun), FadeOut(sun_label),
            FadeOut(planet), FadeOut(planet_label),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for multi-word labels
        final_msg = Text("The Geometry of the Universe", color=color_text, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_msg, "B2", "E6")
        
        self.play(Write(final_msg))
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=1)
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # End of section
        self.play(FadeOut(final_msg), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: Prerequisite: The String & The Sphere
outline.content: Review two crucial geometric rules: 1. The definition of an ellipse (the sum of distances to two fixed foci is constant). 2. The Tangent Segment Theorem (tangent lines drawn from a single point to a sphere are always equal in length).
outline.example: Visualizing a gardener using a loose loop of string around two pegs to draw a flowerbed, followed by a 3D animation showing two tangent lines from a floating point touching a sphere at equal distances.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The String & The Sphere
lecture_lines: Ellipses have two foci with constant distance sum.
Tangents from one point to a sphere are equal.
These rules help unlock the cone's secret.

Draw two yellow lines (#FFFF00) from a point on the curve to the foci using a string [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/string.svg]; show their sum is constant.
Show a blue sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] and demonstrate that all tangent segments from an external point to it are equal length (#00FF00).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: The String & The Sphere"
        lines = [
            "Ellipses have two foci with constant distance sum.",
            "Tangents from one point to a sphere are equal.",
            "These rules help unlock the cone's secret."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Colors
        color_ellipse = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        color_foci = "#FF0000"    # Red
        color_lines = "#FFFF00"   # Yellow
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_ellipse)
        
        # Ellipse
        # Using a=2, b=1.25 -> c = 1.56
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=4.0, height=2.5, color=color_ellipse)
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, 'B2', 'E6')
        center_pos = ellipse.get_center()
        c = 1.56
        
        focus1_pos = center_pos + LEFT * c
        focus2_pos = center_pos + RIGHT * c
        
        focus1 = Dot(focus1_pos, color=color_foci)
        focus2 = Dot(focus2_pos, color=color_foci)
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for multi-word Text labels
        foci_label = Text("Foci Locations", font_size=24, color=color_foci)
        self.place_in_area(foci_label, 'A3', 'A5')
        
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.play(FadeIn(focus1, focus2), Write(foci_label))
        
        # Constant sum demonstration
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(PI/4)
        
        def get_point_on_ellipse():
            theta = angle_tracker.get_value()
            return center_pos + np.array([2 * np.cos(theta), 1.25 * np.sin(theta), 0])
        
        moving_point = Dot(get_point_on_ellipse(), color=WHITE)
        moving_point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_point_on_ellipse()))
        
        line1 = Line(focus1_pos, get_point_on_ellipse(), color=color_lines)
        line2 = Line(focus2_pos, get_point_on_ellipse(), color=color_lines)
        
        line1.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([focus1_pos, get_point_on_ellipse()]))
        line2.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([focus2_pos, get_point_on_ellipse()]))
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for long MathTex expressions
        sum_text = MathTex("d_1 + d_2 = \\text{constant}", font_size=32, color=color_lines)
        self.place_in_area(sum_text, 'F2', 'F6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(moving_point, line1, line2), Write(sum_text))
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/4 + 2*PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        color_sphere = "#0000FF"   # Blue
        color_tangent = "#00FF00"  # Green
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_sphere),
            FadeOut(ellipse, focus1, focus2, foci_label, moving_point, line1, line2, sum_text)
        )
        
        # "Sphere"
        sphere = Circle(radius=1.5, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sphere.set_fill(color_sphere, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'B3', 'E5')
        sphere_center = sphere.get_center()
        
        # External Point
        # B021: Maintain gap from lecture text (Column 1)
        p_pos = self.grid['C6']
        point_p = Dot(p_pos, color=WHITE)
        
        # Calculate Tangent Points
        d_val = np.linalg.norm(p_pos - sphere_center)
        r_val = 1.5
        local_p = p_pos - sphere_center
        angle_p = np.arctan2(local_p[1], local_p[0])
        alpha = np.arccos(r_val / d_val)
        
        t1_pos = sphere_center + np.array([r_val * np.cos(angle_p + alpha), r_val * np.sin(angle_p + alpha), 0])
        t2_pos = sphere_center + np.array([r_val * np.cos(angle_p - alpha), r_val * np.sin(angle_p - alpha), 0])
        
        tangent1 = Line(p_pos, t1_pos, color=color_tangent)
        tangent2 = Line(p_pos, t2_pos, color=color_tangent)
        
        l1_label = MathTex("L_1", font_size=28, color=color_tangent).next_to(tangent1, UP, buff=0.1)
        l2_label = MathTex("L_2", font_size=28, color=color_tangent).next_to(tangent2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        equal_text = MathTex("L_1 = L_2", font_size=32, color=color_tangent)
        self.place_in_area(equal_text, 'F3', 'F5')
        
        sphere_label = Text("3D Sphere Model", font_size=24, color=color_sphere)
        self.place_in_area(sphere_label, 'A3', 'A5')

        self.play(Create(sphere), Write(sphere_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(point_p))
        self.play(Create(tangent1), Create(tangent2))
        self.play(Write(l1_label), Write(l2_label))
        self.play(Write(equal_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup or hold
        self.play(FadeOut(sphere, sphere_label, point_p, tangent1, tangent2, l1_label, l2_label, equal_text))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "The Magic Trick: Inserting the Spheres"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Nest two spheres between the cone and plane.",
            "Plane contact points will become our two foci.",
            "We call these the Dandelin Spheres."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Define colors
        CONE_COLOR = "#888888"
        PLANE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        SPHERE_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        FOCI_COLOR = "#FF0000"

        # 3D Construction Group
        # Since we are in a 2D Scene, we'll use a VGroup and rotate it to simulate 3D
        three_d_view = VGroup()

        # 1. Cone (Visual representation)
        # We'll use a double cone for the full effect, but focusing on the top part for now
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=4.0, direction=UP, 
                   fill_opacity=0.1, color=CONE_COLOR, stroke_width=1)
        cone.rotate(PI, axis=RIGHT) # Point down for "ice cream cone" feel
        cone.move_to(ORIGIN)
        three_d_view.add(cone)

        # 2. Slicing Plane
        # A tilted plane that intersects the cone
        plane = Rectangle(width=4, height=4, fill_opacity=0.2, 
                          fill_color=PLANE_COLOR, color=PLANE_COLOR)
        plane.rotate(60 * DEGREES, axis=RIGHT)
        plane.rotate(10 * DEGREES, axis=UP)
        plane.move_to(UP * 0.2)
        three_d_view.add(plane)

        # Position the 3D view in the visual area (right side)
        # Area A2 to F6 to respect Belief B021
        self.place_in_area(three_d_view, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # Small Sphere (above plane)
        # Positioned to be tangent to cone walls and plane

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Application: From Ice Cones to Orbits"
        lines = [
            "Tilting the plane creates other conic sections.",
            "This geometry governs how planets orbit stars.",
            "3D shapes explain our 2D mathematical world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors from animation description
        color_parabola = "#FF00FF"
        color_hyperbola = "#00FF00"
        color_planet = "#ADD8E6"
        color_sun = "#FFFF00"
        color_text = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Representing a cone via cross-section
        cone_l = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F2"], color=GREY_B)
        cone_r = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F6"], color=GREY_B)
        cone = VGroup(cone_l, cone_r)
        
        # Slicing Plane line
        plane = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D5"], color=WHITE)
        plane_label = Text("Plane", font_size=18).next_to(plane, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(cone), Create(plane), Write(plane_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Parabola Animation
        # Define a parabola relative to the grid
        parabola = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.8 * x**2 - 0.5, 
            x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], 
            color=color_parabola
        )
        self.place_in_area(parabola, "C3", "E5")
        parabola_label = Text("Parabola", color=color_parabola, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6),
            FadeIn(parabola),
            Write(parabola_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Hyperbola Animation
        hyperbola_top = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.3), 
            x_range=[-1, 1], 
            color=color_hyperbola
        )
        hyperbola_bot = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: -np.sqrt(x**2 + 0.3), 
            x_range=[-1, 1], 
            color=color_hyperbola
        )
        hyperbola = VGroup(hyperbola_top, hyperbola_bot)
        self.place_in_area(hyperbola, "C3", "E5")
        
        hyperbola_label = Text("Hyperbola", color=color_hyperbola, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6),
            FadeOut(parabola),
            FadeOut(parabola_label),
            FadeIn(hyperbola),
            Write(hyperbola_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup for transition
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cone), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(plane_label),
            FadeOut(hyperbola), FadeOut(hyperbola_label),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Orbital system
        # Center of ellipse at D4, Sun at focus D3 (distance = 1.0)
        # a=1.5, c=1.0 => b = sqrt(1.5^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(1.25) approx 1.118
        # width = 2a = 3.0, height = 2b = 2.236
        orbit_path = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=2.236, color=BLUE_E).set_stroke(opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(orbit_path, "D4")
        
        sun = Dot(color=color_sun, radius=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(sun, "D3") # Focus
        sun_label = Text("Sun", color=color_sun, font_size=20).next_to(sun, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        planet = Dot(color=color_planet, radius=0.12)
        planet_label = Text("Planet", color=color_planet, font_size=18)
        
        # Setup orbital movement
        orbit_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        planet.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(orbit_path.point_from_proportion(orbit_tracker.get_value() % 1)))
        planet_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(planet, UR, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(Create(orbit_path), FadeIn(sun), Write(sun_label))
        self.add(planet, planet_label)
        self.play(orbit_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(orbit_path), FadeOut(sun), FadeOut(sun_label),
            FadeOut(planet), FadeOut(planet_label),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # B002: Use place_in_area for multi-word labels
        final_msg = Text("The Geometry of the Universe", color=color_text, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(final_msg, "B2", "E6")
        
        self.play(Write(final_msg))
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=1)
        self.play(final_msg.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # End of section
        self.play(FadeOut(final_msg), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: The Grand Proof
outline.content: Demonstrate that the sum of the distances from point P to both spheres' contact points (PF1 + PF2) is equal to the fixed distance between the two 'rim' circles along the cone's slant height. Since this distance doesn't change regardless of where P is, the curve is proven to be an ellipse.
outline.example: The two segments PF1 and PF2 are highlighted in glowing colors. As P moves around the ellipse, the total length of the 'glowing line' stays perfectly constant, matching a fixed segment on the cone's wall.

storyboard.title: The Grand Proof
lecture_lines: Sum the distances from P to both foci.
This sum equals a fixed cone slant distance.
Slant distance between spheres never changes.
Thus, the total distance from P is constant.
This proves the curve is a perfect ellipse.
animations: Show that PF1 equals the segment from P to the top circle (Q1).
Show that PF2 equals the segment from P to the bottom circle (Q2).
Combine these to show PF1 + PF2 = Q1Q2, which is the slant distance between the two circles.
Slide point P around the ellipse; show the distance Q1Q2 between circles stays constant.
Display 'Constant Sum = Ellipse' (#FFFFFF) with a celebratory glow on the curve.

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        self.setup_layout("The Grand Proof", [
            "Sum the distances from P to both foci.",
            "This sum equals a fixed cone slant distance.",
            "Slant distance between spheres never changes.",
            "Thus, the total distance from P is constant.",
            "This proves the curve is a perfect ellipse."
        ])

        # Define basic geometry colors
        color_p = WHITE
        color_f1 = TEAL
        color_f2 = YELLOW
        color_plane = ORANGE
        color_cone = GREY_B
        color_sphere = GREY_D
        color_slant = PURPLE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Cone cross-section
        apex = self.grid["A4"]
        wall_l = Line(apex, self.grid["F2"], color=color_cone)
        wall_r = Line(apex, self.grid["F6"], color=color_cone)
        self.add(wall_l, wall_r)

        # Plane line (representing the ellipse)
        plane_start = self.grid["B3"]
        plane_end = self.grid["E5"]
        plane_line = Line(plane_start, plane_end, color=color_plane)
        self.add(plane_line)

        # Spheres (Circles tangent to walls and plane)
        # Manually positioned for visual clarity
        s1_center = self.grid["B4"] + DOWN * 0.1
        s1 = Circle(radius=0.45, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(s1_center)
        s2_center = self.grid["D4"] + DOWN * 0.35
        s2 = Circle(radius=0.85, color=color_sphere, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(s2_center)
        self.add(s1, s2)

        # Focal points (where spheres touch the plane)
        f1_pos = plane_line.point_from_proportion(0.2)
        f2_pos = plane_line.point_from_proportion(0.8)
        f1 = Dot(f1_pos, color=color_f1)
        f2 = Dot(f2_pos, color=color_f2)
        f1_label = MathTex("F_1", color=color_f1, font_size=20).next_to(f1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        f2_label = MathTex("F_2", color=color_f2, font_size=20).next_to(f2, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Point P on the ellipse
        p_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        p_dot = Dot(color=color_p)
        p_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(plane_line.point_from_proportion(p_tracker.get_value())))
        p_label = MathTex("P", color=color_p, font_size=24)
        p_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(p_dot, UP, buff=0.1))

        # PF1 and PF2 segments
        pf1_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(p_dot.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color=color_f1, stroke_width=4))
        pf2_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(p_dot.get_center(), f2.get_center(), color=color_f2, stroke_width=4))

        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_f1)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(f1, f1_label, f2, f2_label, p_dot, p_label),
            Create(pf1_line),
            Create(pf2_line)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Introduce points Q1 and Q2 on the slant height
        # In Dandelin's proof, PF1 = PQ1 and PF2 = PQ2 where Q is on the rim circles.
        # We visualize these Q points on the wall generator.
        
        # Q1 and Q2 on the wall (rim circle contact points)
        q1_pos = wall_l.point_from_proportion(0.25)
        q2_pos = wall_l.point_from_proportion(0.75)
        q1 = Dot(q1_pos, color=color_f1)
        q2 = Dot(q2_pos, color=color_f2)
        q1_label = MathTex("Q_1", color=color_f1, font_size=20).next_to(q1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        q2_label = MathTex("Q_2", color=color_f2, font_size=20).next_to(q2, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # PQ1 and PQ2 as dashed segments to show mapping (Tangent Equality)
        pq1_line = always_redraw(lambda: DashedLine(p_dot.get_center(), q1.get_center(), color=color_f1, dash_length=0.1))
        pq2_line = always_redraw(lambda: DashedLine(p_dot.get_center(), q2.get_center(), color=color_f2, dash_length=0.1))

        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.play(FadeIn(q1, q1_label, q2, q2_label), Create(pq1_line), Create(pq2_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The distance Q1Q2 along the slant height is fixed
        slant_segment = Line(q1_pos, q2_pos, color=color_slant, stroke_width=6)
        slant_label = MathTex("Q_1Q_2", color=color_slant, font_size=24).next_to(slant_segment, LEFT, buff=0.2)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_slant)
        self.play(Create(slant_segment), FadeIn(slant_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Proof: PF1 + PF2 = PQ1 + PQ2 = Q1Q2
        proof_formula = MathTex("PF_1 + PF_2 = PQ_1 + PQ_2 = Q_1Q_2", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(proof_formula, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Write(proof_formula))
        
        # Animate P moving to show that while PF1 and PF2 change, the logic holds
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.3), run_time=1.5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.play(p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.7), run_time=1.5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Concluding statement with celebratory glow
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GOLD)
        conclusion = Text("Constant Sum = Ellipse", color=GOLD, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(conclusion, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Highlight the ellipse (plane line)
        ellipse_glow = plane_line.copy().set_stroke(GOLD, width=12, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(
            Write(conclusion),
            Create(ellipse_glow),
            p_tracker.animate.set_value(0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data for the scene
        title = "The Mystery of the Slice"
        lines = [
            "- Imagine slicing a cone with a flat plane.",
            "- This intersection creates a perfect elliptical curve.",
            "- Why does this slice follow the ellipse formula?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        CONE_COLOR = "#888888"
        PLANE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        SLICE_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        TEXT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Imagine slicing a cone with a flat plane.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a 2D perspective representation of a cone
        cone_base = Ellipse(width=3, height=0.6, color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        cone_base.shift(DOWN * 1.5)
        cone_sides = Polygon([-1.5, -1.5, 0], [0, 1.5, 0], [1.5, -1.5, 0], color=CONE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.1)
        cone = VGroup(cone_sides, cone_base)
        self.place_in_area(cone, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Create a slicing plane (parallelogram)
        plane = Polygon(
            [-2.5, 0.5, 0], [1.5, 1.5, 0], [2.5, -0.5, 0], [-1.5, -1.5, 0],
            color=PLANE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        # Visual adjustment to make it look like it's intersecting the middle
        plane.shift(UP * 0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), FadeIn(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # This intersection creates a perfect elliptical curve.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Tilted ellipse representing the slice
        slice_curve = Ellipse(width=1.6, height=0.6, color=SLICE_COLOR, stroke_width=5)
        slice_curve.rotate(14 * DEGREES)
        self.place_in_area(slice_curve, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        slice_curve.shift(UP * 0.4 + RIGHT * 0.1) # Align with the plane's tilt
        
        self.play(Create(slice_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Why does this slice follow the ellipse formula?
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Simulate camera rotation: transform components to face-on view
        # The slice becomes a standard oval
        final_ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.5, height=2.2, color=SLICE_COLOR, stroke_width=5)
        self.place_in_area(final_ellipse, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Rotate the view: 
        # 1. Transform the slice to look flat
        # 2. Fade out the cone and plane
        self.play(
            Transform(slice_curve, final_ellipse),
            cone.animate.set_opacity(0),
            plane.animate.set_opacity(0),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.remove(cone, plane)
        
        # Final Question Text (Applying B002: Span multiple columns)
        question_text = Text("Why is this an Ellipse?", font_size=24, color=TEXT_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(question_text, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(question_text))
        self.wait(2)

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
